clue.text: Horrible person, intellectual of a certain hue?

parts.note: a pig is a nasty, greedy person
mental means of the intellect

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a brainy person with an odd skin colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: pigmental means relating to pigment, so concerned with colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigment is the substance giving colour, so pigmental loosely describes something to do with a particular colouring.

clue.text: Maiden rushed up to meet the first person in embrace

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun
ran, turned upwards
M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden

explanation.surface: A young woman runs up to greet the speaker with a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Inarm is a poetic verb meaning to clasp in one's arms.

clue.text: Highland assistant that is buried under wooded glen

indicators.note: in a down clue lying under something means coming after it

parts.note: a gill is a wooded ravine
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Highland helper lies buried beneath a forested valley.
explanation.walkthrough: A gillie works for anglers or deer-stalkers on Scottish estates.
explanation.definitionFit: A gillie is a Highland attendant who helps sportsmen when fishing or hunting.

clue.text: African islander, once a prisoner in crushed condition

indicators.note: one thing placed in another goes inside it

parts.note: a mash is a crushed pulpy state
taken as written
a lag is a convict

explanation.surface: An African islander who used to be a convict is now squashed flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' belongs to the definition, since Malagash is an old form of Malagasy; it does not mean former prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Malagash is an obsolete name for a native of Madagascar, the island off Africa.

clue.text: Indonesian den, one with nothing inside

indicators.note: the letters go inside the word for a lair

parts.note: a nest is an animal's den
I is the Roman numeral one
nothing is zero, O

explanation.surface: An Indonesian lair with a single occupant and nothing else in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesiot, from Greek for islander, is Chambers' word for a native of the Indonesian archipelago.

clue.text: Sailors coming to American city where saint was born

parts.note: tars are sailors
US is the United States, so American

explanation.surface: Seamen arrive at a US town that was a saint's birthplace.
explanation.walkthrough: The saint is Paul, known as Saul of Tarsus before his conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsus, in modern Turkey, was the birthplace of the apostle Paul.

clue.text: Helps when chance has to be seized

indicators.note: something seized is held in the grip of something else, so it goes inside

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a bet is a chance taken on an outcome

explanation.surface: Someone lends a hand whenever an opportunity must be grabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Like colourful festival, free for all

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and can move

parts.note: the letters of for all rearranged

explanation.surface: A bright carnival open to everyone at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral means of or decked with flowers, as a flower festival is.

clue.text: Mountain sheep loves to look down on valley and lake

indicators.note: in a down clue the part that looks down from above is placed first

parts.note: love is zero, O, here twice
a ria is a drowned river valley
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A wild sheep enjoys gazing from the heights over a valley and lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The oorial, or urial, is a wild sheep of the mountains of central Asia.

clue.text: Philanderer more prudent going round Arab land

indicators.note: going round something encircles it

parts.note: wiser means more sensible
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A sensible flirt travels around an Arab country.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser chases many women, as a philanderer does.

clue.text: A Parisian, I had to be member of a church

parts.note: un is French for a
taken as written
to have a meal is to eat, so had can mean ate

explanation.surface: A Parisian speaker explains how they came to join a congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Uniate belongs to an Eastern church in communion with Rome while keeping its own rites.

clue.text: Indian animal that's awful crossing a lake

indicators.note: crossing over something spans it, so the outer word straddles the inner letters

parts.note: boo is the cry a crowd makes at something awful
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Some beast in India is so dreadful it has to swim across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Baloo, the bear in The Jungle Book, takes his name from the Hindi word for bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Baloo is an Indian word for a bear, recorded in Chambers as an animal of India.

clue.text: Phone America for something to help broken bones

parts.note: to phone someone is to call them
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A patient rings the States hoping for a cure for fractures.
explanation.definitionFit: A callus is the hard tissue that forms around a fracture and knits the broken bone together.

clue.text: Class with Scripture etc making one behave better

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject covering Scripture and the like
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A school claims its Bible lessons improve pupils' conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, religious education, is the British school subject; form is the British word for a school year group.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to mend one's ways and start acting more properly than before.

clue.text: Corrupt celebrity in ill setting

indicators.note: a setting surrounds what is placed in it, as a mount holds a jewel

parts.note: ill as an adverb means badly
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A crooked famous figure is shown in a poor light.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastardly means debased or spurious, in the old sense of corrupted.

clue.text: Plant with bacterial disease — leaf's beginning to wither

indicators.note: one letter goes over to another, so the opening letter is swapped for a new one

parts.note: listeria is a bacterium causing food poisoning

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, used for both words here

parts.note: the first letter of leaf, which is taken out
the first letter of wither, which replaces it

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant has caught a disease and its leaves are starting to droop.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the first letter of LISTERIA from L to W to get WISTERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a climbing shrub with hanging clusters of lilac flowers.

clue.text: A short time entertaining one good chum abroad

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them in, so the inner letters go inside

parts.note: taken as written
mo is short for moment
I is the Roman numeral one
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone briefly hosts a good friend from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, so it is a pal as said in a foreign country.

clue.text: Strawberry about to be munched — the fellow's to eat it

indicators.note: munched food is chewed up and mixed about, so the letters are jumbled
eating something takes it inside, and it points back to the munched letters

parts.note: his is the possessive for a fellow
the letters of about rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is about to chew a strawberry he means to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The hautbois is a tall European strawberry with musky-flavoured fruit.

clue.text: Cent in terrible state, coin no longer usable

indicators.note: something in a terrible condition is in disorder, so its letters are jumbled
one thing set within another goes inside it

parts.note: the letters of state rearranged
C is the abbreviation for cent

explanation.surface: A single cent in poor condition is a coin that can no longer be spent.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceatt was a small silver Anglo-Saxon coin, long out of circulation.

clue.text: Fabric is brought round to be displayed outside room

being outside something means wrapping around it

parts.note: the word is, turned round
a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: Cloth is brought back and hung up outside a room.

clue.text: Around home let's spread cheap decoration

indicators.note: spreading things out scatters them, so the letters are rearranged
going around something encloses it

parts.note: the letters of lets rearranged
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Someone proposes draping cheap trimmings all round the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is glittering metallic strands used as inexpensive Christmas ornament, hence also anything showy but cheap.

clue.text: Ignore little old cutie getting sozzled

indicators.note: someone sozzled is drunk and reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: O is the short form of old
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to the old sweetheart who is getting drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice someone out is to freeze them out, deliberately snubbing them.

clue.text: Non-flying bird needs help — one taken outside to go up

indicators.note: something taken outside goes round the other piece
in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: un is a dialect word for one, as in 'a good un'
to lend a hand is to help

explanation.surface: A flightless bird requires assistance from someone to get airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: Nhandu is another name for the rhea, the large flightless bird of South America.

clue.text: What one is looking for in new role is to kill time

indicators.note: something new is made fresh, so these letters take a different order
one thing placed in another goes inside it

parts.note: the letters of role rearranged
when the sought thing turns up, one says 'this is it'

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for a fresh job is just passing the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to dawdle about idly, letting time pass without purpose.

clue.text: Prostitutes having game start to linger repeatedly in back street

indicators.note: going back means reading the abbreviation the other way
one part placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, written backwards
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of linger, twice

explanation.surface: Streetwalkers hang about in a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-letter abbreviation for street, turned round, is the outer pair; RU and two Ls go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Trull is an archaic word for a harlot or strumpet.

clue.text: Muscular youngster (old-fashioned type) has cut in

to hew is to cut

explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were a British youth fashion of the 1950s, often shortened to Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: Thews are muscles or sinews, so thewed means well-muscled.

clue.text: Early woman, evil ultimately — I left husband, it is gathered

indicators.note: something gathered in is drawn inside the other letters

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of evil
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman of old confesses that, being wicked, she walked out on her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Lilith fits the surface well: in legend she left Adam, her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish legend Lilith was Adam's first wife, created before Eve.

clue.text: Good material that adds a certain gloss

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
lace is a fabric

explanation.definitionFit: Glacé describes a glazed, glossy finish, as on glacé kid leather or glacé icing.

clue.text: Sends back a wee amount

clue.text: African with long hair hugging duke

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair

clue.text: True stories coming from couples once more

explanation.walkthrough: 'True stories' reads as a phrase but splits into two opposites; the answer is RE-ALLIES, not related to really.
explanation.definitionFit: To really is to ally again, so it joins two parties together a second time.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing to be stupid as before, having adopted new name

clue.text: Initial earnings with a debit to be arranged

clue.text: Transvestites in red dancing in parties
